elements.quote: Finally, analysis of these data showed that passive immunization (SMD=0.87; 95%CI: 0.19-1.55; p=0.012) and active immunization (SMD=2.08, 95%CI: 1.42-2.73; p<0.001) for/with MBP both have good efficacy in improving locomotion following traumatic SCI.

elements.quote: ...both have good efficacy in improving locomotion following traumatic SCI.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (improving locomotion) and implies the immunization group is favored.

elements.quote: However, significant heterogeneity was observed in both of them. ... Although, there was substantial heterogeneity among studies...
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes limitations regarding inconsistency (heterogeneity).

elements.quote: Conclusion: The results of the present study demonstrated that immunization with MBP , especially in its active form, could significantly improve motor function following SCI in rats and mice. Therefore, it could be considered as a potential treatment in acute settings such as emergency departments.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications in the Conclusion section.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: However, there is still significant disagreement over the new treatment strategies. For instance, older studies had demonstrated that inflammation caused by autoimmune response leads to exacerbation of SCI and motor impairment (6, 7). Nonetheless, recent animal research showed that the postinjury autoimmune reactions provoke beneficial endogenous responses following SCI (8)... Although several studies that evaluate the effectiveness of active and passive immunization in SCI are available, conflicting findings have been reported between studies.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge regarding SCI treatments and immune response, and highlights important uncertainties such as disagreement over strategies and conflicting findings between studies.

elements.quote: Current treatments have very low efficacy and can only alleviate some of its symptoms... On the other hand, it is not yet clear which active and inactive immunogenic methods are more effective in improving the motor function of animals. Accordingly, there is still no conclusion on the role of passive immunization... Hence, the present study aims to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the effectiveness...
elements.reason: The text explains the importance of the review by noting the low efficacy of current treatments and the need to resolve conflicting findings and lack of conclusions in the literature.

elements.quote: Accordingly, there is still no conclusion on the role of passive immunization with immune cells activated by MBP or on active immunization with injection of MBP and its derivatives in the treatment of SCI in the literature.
elements.reason: The text states there is 'no conclusion... in the literature', implying no previous systematic review has resolved the issue, thus the requirement to explain the need relative to existing reviews does not apply.

elements.quote: Myelin Basic Protein (MBP) is a surface antigen expressed on cells in the CNS. Available studies show that transplantation of activated immune cells against this antigen is associated with improved motor recovery in animals with SCI... It has also been demonstrated that proper regulation of immune response following SCI may have an essential role in axonal regeneration...
elements.reason: The text briefly describes the proposed mechanism of action, explaining that MBP is an antigen and that immune regulation plays a role in axonal regeneration and recovery.

elements.quote: Active and Passive Immunization with Myelin Basic Protein as a Method for Early Treatment of Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury
elements.reason: The intervention (immunization with MBP) is a standard biological intervention and not described as a complex intervention requiring a logic model to show hypothesised relationships between components.

elements.quote: PICO was defined as follows: Problem (P) included animals in which SCI injury was induced. Intervention (I) was the injection of MBP-activated T cells (passive immunization) or administration of MBP or MBP-modified peptides, inducing intrinsic immunity to MBP (active immunization). Comparison (C) consisted of a comparison with control animals, which were induced with SCI but had not received treatment, and outcome (O) was an assessment of motor function by BBB testing.
elements.reason: The review objectives/questions are explicitly stated using the PICO framework in the Methods section, defining the problem, intervention, comparison, and outcome.
